notes.decision: Page number ⲥ̄ (=200) is preserved partially in the manuscript; canonical reading for this page is ⲥⲓ̄ (=210). The transcription brackets [ⲥ] indicate editor restoration of the visible numeral.

Rendered 'The Chapter.' The header is unusually short (no chapter number/title), framed by decorative bookends [> ·] ... · <. May indicate either a chapter divider with title lost, or an interior section marker.
Translated 'shall reach' from ⲧⲉⲍⲟ 'reach, befall' (in glossary) + 3sg.m suffix; future ⲛⲁ-. The sickness 'reaches' the members (befalls them).
Greek loanword λύπη as a stative predicate: 'is in grief.' The article ⲡ̄- here functions predicatively in Lyc., similar to ⲣ̄-ⲗⲩⲧⲏ 'to grieve' (in glossary).
Qualitative/circumstantial 'being pricked' from ⲧⲕⲉⲥ 'sting, prick' (Lyc. = Sah. ⲧⲱⲕⲥ̄, in glossary as 'affliction'). Bodily-medical register: the soul is pricked in the sickness.

ⲧⲱⲕ ⲛ̄ⲍⲏⲧ 'cheering of heart' — ⲧⲱⲕ here likely from ⲧⲱⲕ 'kindle, hearten, encourage' (cf. accumulated ⲡⲱⲕ ⲛⲍⲏⲧ 'purpose of heart' but distinct root). The physician brings cheer (rallying of heart) to the sick.
Rendered 'his salvation/health' (Lyc. = Sah. ⲟⲩϫⲁⲓ 'health, salvation'). The medical-soteriological register fits: physician gives healing/salvation. Possessive ⲡ-ⲟⲩ-ⲭⲉⲓⲧⲉ 'his health.'
Translated 'has befallen him' — ⲛⲉⲍⲥⲉ as a verb of arrival/befalling (possibly Lyc. reflex of ⲛⲉϩⲥⲉ 'wake/come upon' in transferred sense). Confidence moderate.

Translated 'them, calling them' — parsing as object pronoun ⲙⲙⲟⲩ + verbal infinitive ⲧⲉⲙⲟⲩⲧⲉ (or ⲙⲟⲩⲧⲉ 'to call'); alternatively 'the names' (Lyc. plural). The wise man knows-them and calls-them physicians.
Substantival qualitative 'the suffering one' — ⲡⲉⲧ- + ϩⲁⲭ (possibly Lyc. for ϩⲱϫ 'be afflicted, oppressed'). The therapy is 'of the sufferer.'

Translated 'the names' — taking ⲙⲟⲩⲧⲉ here as substantival 'naming/names' rather than infinitive. The physician declares the diagnostic names of the diseases. Alternative 'the gods' is grammatically possible but contextually unlikely.

Substantival 'the other examination' — ⲍⲱⲙ here functioning as a noun parallel to its verbal use throughout the chapter (lines 11, 15, 17, 20, 22, 26). Likely Lyc. reflex of a verb of close inspection/diagnosis (possibly cognate with Sah. ⲥⲱⲙ 'investigate' or ϫⲱⲱⲙⲉ).
Translated 'upon' — Lyc. reflex of ⲉϫⲛ̄ 'upon, over.' The physician's examination of what is upon (i.e. visible in/on) the members.

Rendered 'remove from him' — Lyc. ⲧⲟⲩⲓ̈ⲟ likely from ⲧⲟⲩⲱ/ⲧⲟⲩⲟ 'send forth, expel' (cf. accumulated ⲧⲟⲩⲱ 'raise' — here in horizontal-expulsion sense). The physician removes the sickness from the patient.

Translated 'and to bring forth this profit' — ⲧⲁⲗⲁⲓⲟ̄ⲉ as Lyc. causative 'cause to come up, bring forth' (cf. ⲧⲁⲗⲟ 'mount, raise'). The physician's purpose: to produce profit (ⲡⲍⲏⲩ in glossary) for the sick man.
Translated 'bring forth wrath' — ⲭⲡⲟ (Lyc. ϫⲡⲟ 'beget, bring forth') + ⲛⲉⲟ̈ⲉ 'wrath/anger' (likely Lyc. reflex of ⲛⲟⲩϭⲥ̄ or related anger-noun). Pair-partner with ⲃⲗⲕⲉ 'anger' (line 27 doublet).
Translated 'treachery/plot' — Greek ἐπιβουλία 'plot, malicious design' rendered with Lyc. orthography. Fits the context of the hostile examiner who wishes to add another sickness.

Lexeme uncertain. Tentative reading 'with cover/concealment' or 'under malice'; possibly ϩⲁ- 'under' + ⲃⲓⲱⲡ (root unidentified — possibly cognate with ⲃⲱⲡ 'cover' or related). Left in Coptic in the rendering pending parallel attestations.

Rendered 'the other face' — ⲍⲟ = Lyc. ϩⲟ 'face' (cf. ⲡⲍⲟ in glossary). In this paraphrase of Matt 6:21 ('where your treasure is, there your heart will be'), the saying may be reformulated reciprocally with 'the other face/aspect' substituted for 'treasure.' Alternative reading 'the other treasure' (ⲍⲟ as Lyc. for ⲁϩⲟ) is also possible.

Translated 'to the King' — Lyc. ⲡⲟⲣⲟ = Sah. ⲡⲣ̄ⲣⲟ 'king' (cf. accumulated ⲣ̄ⲡⲟ, ⲡⲓⲣⲡⲟ). The diaeresis ⲟ̈ marks the spelling. The bones afflicted are drawn 'to the King' — to the divine kingship, soteriological terminus.

Reduplicative emphatic phrase across the line break: 'this labor — labor again of the other bones.' ⲍⲁϣ likely = Lyc. for affliction/labor (possibly cognate with ⲍⲱϣ 'afflict' attested in line 30 ⲁⲕⲍⲉϣⲍⲱϣϩ). Rendering both occurrences as 'labor' to preserve the iteration.
